title: Bind forced release replacement to its destination
summary: Require destination-bound release identity before replacing a nonempty release directory and preserve the prior directory in a recoverable sibling quarantine.
reason: Remediate P1 AUDIT-FIND-W10-016. A copied or one-field release marker currently authorizes recursive deletion of any otherwise allowed nonempty directory selected with -Force.
behavior_before: A parseable release_manifest.json or .release_in_progress.json containing only the expected schema version authorizes Remove-Item -Recurse -Force on the selected destination.
behavior_after: A nonempty destination is replaceable only when its partial or completed marker carries a valid build nonce and cryptographic bindings to the exact canonical destination, source root, normalized version, and source revision. Reparse-point path components are rejected. Valid prior output moves atomically to a sibling quarantine, is restored if the rebuild fails, and remains recoverable after success for explicit operator cleanup.
tests_added: Disposable mini-release builds reject completed and partial schema-only markers while preserving unrelated files.
Copied markers and destination, source-root, normalized-version, or source-revision identity mismatches fail closed and preserve unrelated contents.
A valid custom destination replacement preserves the old tree in a sibling quarantine.
A forced post-quarantine copy failure restores the prior destination and preserves partial output separately.
A junction destination is rejected before replacement and its target contents remain unchanged.
manual_validation: PowerShell parsing passed for the release builder and owning release-package policy test.
